questions.label: Practice · An 81-year-old man has burning pain and allodynia in the left T10 dermatome six months after herpes zoster. Gabapentin and duloxetine have not helped. He has COPD, atrial fibrillation treated with apixaban, and stage 3 CKD; other medications are metoprolol, tiotropium, and acetaminophen. The pain prevents him from hugging his grandchildren. Which listed coanalgesic appears as a topical patch option in Hazzard’s Table 68-8?

Practice · A 74-year-old woman with depression and osteoarthritis has persistent hip pain despite acetaminophen. She takes sertraline and declines NSAIDs because of gastrointestinal concerns. The team is considering a supervised change to duloxetine. Which source-described action explains its potential analgesic role?

Practice · A 76-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and chronic back pain has become sedentary and mentally foggy despite physical therapy. He takes duloxetine, cyclobenzaprine, and acetaminophen. Which medication change best reduces his anticholinergic and sedative burden?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 24) and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) is hospitalized with pneumonia. On day three she develops acute confusion, visual hallucinations, and agitation; the CAM is positive. She pulls at an indwelling urinary catheter that is no longer medically needed. She is receiving levofloxacin, acetaminophen, amlodipine, and atorvastatin. Which initial intervention best follows Hazzard’s nonpharmacologic approach?

Practice · An 82-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced dementia and breast cancer metastatic to bone presents with two days of shouting, agitation, food refusal, and pulling at her clothes. She is nonverbal at baseline and grimaces during abdominal palpation. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, heart rate 88, and blood pressure 142/78. She receives memantine 10 mg twice daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. Which approach best addresses the acute behavioral change?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment, hypertension, and osteoarthritis attends routine follow-up. Her daughter reports frequent liquid stool soiling despite complaints of constipation. Medications include amlodipine 5 mg, acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and docusate 100 mg twice daily. Digital rectal examination reveals a large mass of hard stool in the rectal vault with liquid stool leaking around it. Lawton-Brody assessment shows new difficulty shopping and preparing meals. What is the preferred initial approach?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman with moderate vascular dementia in a memory-care unit has refused bathing for two weeks and smells of urine. She becomes aggressive when approached with bathing equipment, but there is no immediate danger. She has hypertension and osteoarthritis and takes amlodipine 5 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg twice daily. Her daughter says she used to be meticulous about cleanliness. Alongside assessing causes of distress, which approach follows first-line behavioral care?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with hypertension and osteoarthritis develops fatigue and exertional dyspnea after starting meloxicam for knee pain. Hemoglobin is 8.2 g/dL, MCV 78 fL, ferritin 18 ng/mL, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL from 1.1, and eGFR 32 mL/min/1.73 m². Stool testing is positive for blood and colonoscopy shows a bleeding diverticulum. After the acute bleed is treated, which analgesic principle follows Hazzard's discussion of safer prescribing for osteoarthritis?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter and needs help with IADLs. On the third hospital day for pneumonia she is more confused at night, sleeps during the day, is oriented to person, and picks at unseen objects. CAM is positive. She receives ceftriaxone 1 g daily and acetaminophen as needed. Alongside evaluating and treating causes, which environmental approach is consistent with delirium and sleep-wake management?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with severe osteoarthritis and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52; Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance 38) has inadequate relief from acetaminophen 1 g three times daily. She has hypertension and heart failure with an ejection fraction of 45%, and takes lisinopril, carvedilol, and furosemide. If an opioid trial is warranted after other treatments have been reviewed, which agent does Hazzard place before other opioids?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with Alzheimer dementia (MMSE 14) and osteoarthritis has fallen twice in the past month without injury. She inconsistently uses a walker. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg four times daily; amitriptyline 25 mg nightly was added for sleep six weeks ago. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/68 after three minutes standing; pulse rises from 72 to 78. Which medication change best addresses the timing of the falls and the postural pressure drop?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman hospitalized with pneumonia becomes irritable on the third hospital day, grimaces with movement, and resists care. She has moderate dementia, a positive delirium screen, and difficulty localizing her reported severe generalized pain. Temperature is 37.8°C, heart rate 102, and blood pressure 160/95. Her home medications include donepezil, amlodipine, and acetaminophen 500 mg twice daily for arthritis. While evaluating the new pain and delirium, the team considers acetaminophen as one component of treatment for her osteoarthritis pain. Which approach follows Hazzard’s discussion of this drug?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with hypertension, diabetes, osteoarthritis, and newly diagnosed mild cognitive impairment takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, celecoxib 200 mg daily, and acetaminophen 500 mg four times daily. She develops ankle edema, an eight-pound weight gain over two weeks, and worsening knee pain. Blood pressure is 165/95 mm Hg, pulse 88/min, and creatinine has risen from 1.1 to 1.4 mg/dL. Which change directly removes an NSAID exposure while retaining a non-NSAID analgesic strategy?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman with diabetes, stage 4 CKD, and peripheral neuropathy has severe burning foot pain despite gabapentin and acetaminophen. She has also developed confusion and fallen. Which step best applies Hazzard's medication-safety principles before adding or escalating treatment?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with chronic low-back pain has marked lumbar facet arthropathy on MRI, local facet tenderness, and pain on extension and lateral rotation. She has hypertension and osteoporosis and takes amlodipine, alendronate, and acetaminophen. Physical therapy gave little relief, and tramadol caused nausea. Which description of medial branch blocks agrees with Hazzard?

Practice · אישה בת 84 עם יתר לחץ דם, כאב כרוני עקב היצרות עמוד השדרה, ו-MCI שאובחן לאחרונה, מגיעה עם בתה לחידוש מרשמים. היא נוטלת amlodipine 5mg, gabapentin 300mg TID, ו-acetaminophen PRN. הבת עונה על כל השאלות ומפסיקה את המטופלת בכל פעם שהיא מנסה לדבר. כשנשאלת על שליטה בכאב, המטופלת מתחילה לענות אך הבת מתערבת ואומרת 'היא בסדר, היא מתלוננת יותר מדי.' המטופלת מורידה את עיניה ומפסיקה לדבר. איזה סוג של התעללות הכי סביר במקרה זה?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer disease and osteoarthritis has increased evening confusion and fell a week ago. He takes donepezil 10 mg nightly, memantine 10 mg twice daily, acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and amitriptyline 50 mg nightly for chronic pain. Which action directly addresses a strongly anticholinergic medication exposure?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%), mild cognitive impairment, and knee osteoarthritis is hospitalized with decompensated heart failure. She lives alone and is independent in four of six activities of daily living. Her discharge medications include furosemide 40 mg twice daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, and naproxen 500 mg twice daily for knee pain. Creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL and eGFR is 28 mL/min/1.73 m². If an oral analgesic is still needed after non-drug measures, which initial change best fits the approach on Hazzard p312?
Practice · A care-home resident with dementia and behavioral problems is assessed for possible pain. What was the first step in the empiric stepwise pain-treatment protocol described in Hazzard?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman with heart failure, mild dementia, and osteoarthritis presents with weight loss and fatigue. After a fall, she moved in with her daughter. She takes furosemide, lisinopril, donepezil, and acetaminophen. She eats less and needs medication reminders. Her weight fell from 58 to 52 kg in six months; albumin is 3.0 and thyroid function is normal. Which approach reflects comprehensive geriatric assessment?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with mild Alzheimer dementia and osteoarthritis spends more time in bed, eats less, and has lost interest in weekly card games. She has near-falls when reaching, temporal wasting, loose clothing, and difficulty rising from the examination table. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. She has lost 12 lb (8%) in six months; TSH is normal, B12 is 320 pg/mL, and albumin is 3.4 g/dL. Which exercise prescription best addresses her weakness?

Practice · An 85-year-old assisted-living resident with moderate Alzheimer disease is on day three after hip-fracture repair. After sleeping well on earlier nights, she is now awake, repeatedly getting out of bed, and saying she must get the children ready for school. She takes memantine 10 mg twice daily, vitamin D, acetaminophen as needed, and zolpidem 5 mg at bedtime added last night. Vital signs are normal. Which medication change follows Beers 2023 guidance for the new delirium?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman in assisted living is assessed because her care needs have increased. She has moderate Alzheimer disease, osteoporosis with a recent vertebral fracture, and urinary incontinence. Her caregiver reports new dependence in bathing and dressing, previously performed independently, and two falls this month. Her medicines are donepezil 10 mg daily, alendronate 70 mg weekly, oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, and acetaminophen as needed. Which response to oxybutynin matches Beers 2023?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, hypertension and osteoarthritis is assessed after a fall in assisted living. He takes carbidopa/levodopa, amlodipine and as-needed acetaminophen. Examination shows masked facies and cogwheel rigidity, with a marked fall in blood pressure and dizziness on standing. Which approach fits the described treatment principles for orthostatic hypotension?

Practice · A 73-year-old woman with diabetes and a recent hip replacement has recurrent sudden episodes of syncope lasting 1–2 minutes, followed by full recovery. Her daughter observes pallor during events. Medications include metformin 1000 mg twice daily, apixaban 5 mg twice daily, and oxycodone/acetaminophen as needed. Orthostatic vital signs and the resting ECG are normal. Continuous monitoring records a 4.2-second sinus pause during syncope. Reversible and physiologic causes have been excluded. Which approach to permanent pacing follows Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with BPH and mild Alzheimer dementia develops three days of inattention, agitation and daytime somnolence. He takes tamsulosin, acetaminophen, memantine and diphenhydramine, added one week ago for insomnia. Vital signs are stable. Urinalysis and chest radiography are normal. Which medication change should be prioritized during the delirium evaluation?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman has pain after hip-fracture surgery despite oxycodone. She has mild cognitive impairment and reduced renal function, without known liver disease. The team is reassessing her pain and wants to reduce opioid exposure. Which addition fits the multimodal approach described in Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman with osteoarthritis becomes drowsy while taking oxycodone. The team is reducing it and considering nonopioid treatment. Oral NSAIDs are unsuitable; she has no liver disease and no described neuropathic pain. If treatment continues for a prolonged period, which acetaminophen plan is consistent with the osteoarthritis chapter of Hazzard?

Practice · An older adult with hip osteoarthritis has stable CKD stage IV and an eGFR of 24 cc/min. An oral analgesic is being considered for a brief pain flare; there is no liver disease. Which approach best follows the chapter's renal-safety advice?

Practice · An 83-year-old woman with wet age-related macular degeneration treated with anti-VEGF injections and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24) develops acute delirium during hospitalization for pneumonia. During evening nursing care she becomes agitated, pulls at her gown, and calls for her deceased husband. She takes ceftriaxone, acetaminophen, and artificial tears. Which initial symptom-management approach is appropriate?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with COPD and knee osteoarthritis has persistent knee pain despite acetaminophen. She has fallen twice this month and attributes this to knee pain. She takes tiotropium, albuterol, calcium, and vitamin D, has an MMSE score of 28/30, uses a walker, and has creatinine clearance of 38 mL/min. Which pharmacologic step follows Hazzard’s approach before oral NSAIDs or opioid escalation?

Practice · An 81-year-old assisted-living resident with moderate vascular dementia, diabetes, and osteoarthritis now needs help bathing and dressing, has fallen twice in the past month, and sometimes misses medication. She takes metformin 500 mg twice daily, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, and acetaminophen as needed; HbA1c is 8.2% and creatinine clearance is 38 mL/min. Which description matches the GRACE model being considered to coordinate her care?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with a two-year history of behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia is brought by his daughter for worsening aggression, with compulsive food-taking and inappropriate sexual comments at his nursing facility. Yesterday he pushed another resident who tried to stop him taking dessert. He has hypertension and osteoarthritis, takes lisinopril 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and has an MMSE score of 22/30. Which statement about treatment of the compulsive behavior is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · A 76-year-old woman with hypertension and osteoarthritis has awakened at 3 a.m. nightly for a month. She goes to bed at 9 p.m., falls asleep easily, lies awake from 3 to 5 a.m., and then dozes until 7 a.m. She naps for 30 minutes after lunch. Her medications are lisinopril 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 500 mg three times daily. Her diary records six hours of sleep and 60% sleep efficiency. Which behavioral intervention follows the sleep-restriction approach?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment, hypertension, and osteoarthritis undergoes hip replacement. She takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, acetaminophen 1 g three times daily, and diclofenac 75 mg twice daily. Creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL and creatinine clearance is 28 mL/min. Her preoperative CAM screen was negative; on the first postoperative day she is confused, picks at the sheets, and does not recognize her daughter. Which change follows the renal-function recommendation for NSAIDs in the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · A woman with dementia and a painful fracture continues to show signs of pain despite an adequate trial of acetaminophen. What can be considered next under the stepwise pain-treatment approach described in Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced dementia and hip osteoarthritis cries during routine care, moans during transfers, and resists bathing. Her PAINAD score is 7/10 despite scheduled acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. Her daughter, the health care proxy, fears opioid addiction. Which educational message about persistent pain in dementia is supported by Hazzard?

target.excerpt: Metformin / metformin ER: printed dose lines 500–1000 mg BID, max 2500 mg/d, 500–2000 mg qd — the page does not pair each line to an agent (p1577).

Practice · An 84-year-old man with diabetes, stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) and mild cognitive impairment attends the emergency department after a fall. His daughter reports three falls in the last month and increasing confusion. His medications are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily and zolpidem 10 mg nightly. Blood pressure is 108/65 seated and 92/58 standing; heart rate rises from 72 to 74. Creatinine is 2.8 and glucose is 68. Which action regarding metformin is supported by his renal function?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman who has never smoked has stage IV lung adenocarcinoma, brain metastases, and an EGFR L858R mutation. She takes amlodipine, metformin, and simvastatin, has reduced renal function, and lives independently but has stopped driving because of mild cognitive impairment. Which initial treatment is supported by the FLAURA results described in Hazzard, including improved overall survival and efficacy in CNS metastases?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman has chronic dizziness and recurrent falls, with persistent imbalance worsened by head movement. She takes metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg, simvastatin 40 mg, and meclizine 25 mg three times daily for three months. She has no nystagmus, a normal Romberg test, difficulty with tandem gait, and negative orthostatic measurements. Which strategy follows Hazzard's approach to prolonged vestibular-suppressant use and chronic dizziness?

Practice · A 76-year-old man with diabetes taking metformin develops a severe acute illness with tissue hypoperfusion around the time of surgery. What is the main reason to avoid metformin in this situation?
Practice · An older adult on metformin develops an acute illness with hypoxemia and worsening renal perfusion. Which medication action is appropriate during the acute episode?

Practice · A 75-year-old woman with diabetes, heart failure (ejection fraction 40%), and chronic insomnia still has a sleep latency of 90 minutes despite CBT-I and appropriate sleep hygiene. She takes metformin 500 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. Creatinine is 1.3 mg/dL and eGFR 44 mL/min. Which listed drug is described by Hazzard as a selective melatonin-receptor agonist that reduces sleep latency?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and newly diagnosed paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is being assessed for anticoagulation. Her creatinine clearance is in the 30–49 mL/min range. She takes metformin, glipizide, amlodipine, and metoprolol, lives alone, manages daily tasks independently, and sometimes forgets medication doses. If rivaroxaban is selected, which statement agrees with Hazzard's table?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 48 mL/min/1.73 m²) is assessed before elective hip replacement. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg. Preoperative tests show creatinine 1.45 mg/dL, potassium 4.2, and glucose 156. He lives alone and manages his medications, but his daughter reports that he has recently been forgetting appointments. Which principle should guide the metformin safety review around surgery?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes and mild dementia lives alone. Her A1C is 9.2% on metformin; she forgets medications and meals. Her daughter requests insulin, but the patient does not want injections. Her MMSE is 28/30, although medication tasks require prompting. After reviewing her goals and arranging adherence support, an oral DPP-4 inhibitor is being discussed. Which description of this drug class matches Hazzard?

Practice · A 74-year-old woman with diabetes and HbA1c 7.2% reports dizziness and near-falls. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 5 mg daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily, and recently began tramadol 50 mg three times daily for osteoarthritis pain. Pre-lunch glucose values are 68–75 mg/dL. When reviewing glipizide because of concern about hypoglycemia, which statement follows Hazzard?

Practice · A 68-year-old man has newly diagnosed T1c prostate cancer, PSA 6.2 ng/mL, Gleason score 6, and two positive cores out of twelve. He has controlled diabetes, mild hypertension, takes metformin and lisinopril, and has ECOG performance status 0. He is concerned about quality of life. Which strategy uses scheduled monitoring while retaining the prospect of delayed, potentially curative treatment if progression is detected?

Practice · A 76-year-old man falls while getting out of bed to urinate at night. He has benign prostatic hyperplasia, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment. He takes tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and glipizide 10 mg twice daily. He gets up three or four times nightly. HbA1c is 7.2%, PSA is 3.2, and postvoid residual is 250 mL. Which environmental adaptation is consistent with Hazzard's approach to toileting-related mobility needs and fall hazards?

Practice · A 73-year-old man with diabetes, mild cognitive impairment, and newly diagnosed prostate cancer attends a preoperative geriatric assessment before radical prostatectomy. He lives with his working daughter and manages medications using a pillbox. HbA1c is 7.8%, blood pressure is 145/85, and medications are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. MMSE is 24/30 with impaired executive function. Which perioperative plan addresses the postoperative cognitive risk identified by this assessment?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with COPD, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment lives alone. She uses her albuterol inhaler “when I remember” and reports difficulty with inhaler technique. Her daughter finds expired inhalers and reports two hospitalizations for exacerbations in six months. FEV1 is 48% predicted. Her medications are as-needed albuterol MDI, daily tiotropium HandiHaler, and metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Which intervention addresses her difficulty delivering inhaled bronchodilators?

Practice · An 83-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension is hospitalized for heart failure. A urine culture grows 100,000 CFU/mL of E. coli. She is cognitively intact, afebrile, and has no urinary symptoms. Admission medications are metformin, lisinopril, and furosemide. Discharge is being planned, with no invasive urologic procedure planned. How should the bacteriuria be managed?

Practice · A 78-year-old man has severe right-sided trigeminal neuralgia in the V2 distribution. He stopped gabapentin 300 mg three times daily because of delirium and has stopped shaving and eating solid food because of pain. He also has mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) and type 2 diabetes treated with metformin and glyburide. Which regional block does Hazzard list for maxillary-division trigeminal pain?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 6), heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22) attends follow-up. His wife reports that he falls asleep during meals and forgets medications. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, carvedilol 25 mg twice daily, and furosemide 40 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, potassium 4.8, and creatinine 2.8. Which change addresses the metformin contraindication stated in Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension, and mild cognitive impairment attends routine follow-up. His daughter reports two falls during the past month, both at night while getting up to use the toilet. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, zolpidem 10 mg at bedtime, and aspirin 81 mg daily. Blood pressure is 138/82 sitting and 118/70 after three minutes standing. Which interpretation of zolpidem is consistent with Beers 2023?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with heart failure (EF 35%), permanent atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes is admitted with volume overload. She functions independently, but her daughter reports recent difficulty managing medications. Her medications are carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, furosemide 80 mg twice daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily, renal-adjusted apixaban, and metformin already withheld during acute illness. Potassium is 5.8, creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.3), and BNP 1850. ECG shows atrial fibrillation at 78 beats/min with QRS 118 ms. Which approach to spironolactone follows Hazzard's safety guidance?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has lost about 7 kg in four months. He takes small bites, chews extensively, reports food going 'the wrong way,' and has a wet, gurgly voice after meals. Medications are metformin 500 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily; creatinine clearance is 44 mL/min. Modified barium swallow shows vallecular residue and delayed swallow initiation. Which statement correctly characterizes rehabilitative swallowing therapy considered after this assessment?
Practice · An older adult taking metformin is acutely hospitalized with a major illness causing decreased tissue perfusion. Which treatment decision and reason follow Hazzard?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with diabetes and peripheral neuropathy has worsening burning foot pain for three months. He takes metformin, lisinopril, and aspirin; HbA1c is 8.2%, and monofilament sensation is absent bilaterally. He lives alone and recently stopped driving because of pain. Gabapentin 300 mg three times daily caused severe dizziness. Which listed analgesic option belongs to the serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor class?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment has recurrent falls, reduced activity, and increasing need for help with finances and medications. Examination shows bradykinesia, reduced arm swing, and a positive pull test. He takes metformin and lisinopril. Which assessment specifically investigates a possible blood-pressure or medication contribution to the falls?

Practice · An older adult with stable type 2 diabetes is being considered for oral treatment. There is no acute illness, unstable heart failure, or renal contraindication. Which statement describes the principal glucose-lowering action of metformin in Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 22) presents after 3 days of productive cough, fever and delirium. He has fallen twice that day and missed medications. His usual drugs are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Temperature is 38.8°C, BP 95/60 mmHg, pulse 110/min, respiratory rate 28/min and oxygen saturation 88% on room air. Chest radiography shows right lower-lobe consolidation; WBC is 16.2, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (baseline 1.2) and glucose 340 mg/dL. Oxygenation and hemodynamic support are being addressed. Which infection-directed strategy accords with Hazzard while microbiology results are pending?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, stage 3 CKD (eGFR 45), and recent functional decline is scheduled for MitraClip placement. She now uses a walker and her daughter manages her medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin. She is anxious about general anesthesia. Which procedural plan is described in Hazzard?
Practice · A woman taking metformin is hospitalized with a severe acute illness that reduces tissue perfusion. Which risk explains avoiding metformin in this setting?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with AML in remission after venetoclax/azacitidine, diabetes, and depression has stopped driving and cooking and sleeps much of the day. Her MMSE is 26/30. She takes prophylactic acyclovir, metformin, and long-standing sertraline 100 mg daily. Examination shows psychomotor slowing, and her CBC is normal. If hypothyroidism is being evaluated as a possible contributor, which initial assessment does Hazzard recommend?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes, heart failure (ejection fraction 40%), and mild dementia attends a geriatric clinic. His wife reports two falls in the past month, missed medication despite pill organizers, and inability to manage household finances. She works full time and feels overwhelmed. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. HbA1c is 9.1%, creatinine 1.6, and eGFR 42. Which model explicitly uses protocols addressing medication management, falls, dementia, and caregiver burden?

Practice · A 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and recently diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) receives home-based primary care. Her daughter found her unconscious twice in the past month, both times early in the morning before breakfast. She takes glimepiride 4 mg once daily with breakfast, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Her latest HbA1c is 6.8%, creatinine clearance is 58 mL/min, and prebreakfast fingerstick glucose readings range from 68 to 95 mg/dL. Which approach to the sulfonylurea agrees with Hazzard when hypoglycemia is a concern?

Practice · An older adult develops watery diarrhea and fecal incontinence. Examination finds no fecal impaction. Medication review seeks a direct diarrheal adverse effect rather than constipation with overflow. Which medication fits that mechanism?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, depression, and mild Alzheimer dementia attends a geriatric assessment. Her daughter reports missed medications and two hypoglycemic episodes requiring emergency visits. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. HbA1c is 6.8%, and recorded glucose values range from 65 to 280. Which medication change most directly reduces the risk of another sulfonylurea-related hypoglycemic episode?

Practice · A 72-year-old man reports worsening urinary frequency, nocturia four to five times nightly, and a weak stream for six months. His AUASI is 18. He has hypertension, diabetes, and recent falls, takes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin, and lives alone. Which drug treats BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms through selective alpha-1A blockade?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with hypertension, diabetes, osteoarthritis, and newly diagnosed mild cognitive impairment takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, celecoxib 200 mg daily, and acetaminophen 500 mg four times daily. She develops ankle edema, an eight-pound weight gain over two weeks, and worsening knee pain. Blood pressure is 165/95 mm Hg, pulse 88/min, and creatinine has risen from 1.1 to 1.4 mg/dL. Which change directly removes an NSAID exposure while retaining a non-NSAID analgesic strategy?

Practice · A 73-year-old woman with diabetes is taking metformin and is hospitalized with a major acute illness that may reduce tissue perfusion. Which drug-related concern justifies avoiding metformin in this situation?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter, who has discovered medication errors. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, donepezil 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, blood pressure is 145/85, and eGFR is 48. Which statement correctly identifies the source-described hypoglycemia concern in her oral diabetes regimen?

Practice · אישה בת 79 במוסד סיעודי מפתחת דלקת ריאות אספירטיבית חוזרת. יש לה דמנציה וסקולרית בינונית (MMSE 18/30), סוכרת, ו-CKD שלב 3 (eGFR 45). התרופות הנוכחיות כוללות metformin 500 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg ליום, ו-sertraline 50 mg ליום. בדיקת בליעה בווידאופלואורוסקופיה מראה אספירציה שקטה של נוזלים דקים. קלינאית התקשורת ממליצה על נוזלים סמיכים, אך המטופלת מסרבת. לבתה יש ייפוי כוח מתמשך. מה הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?

Practice · A 78-year-old widower is brought by his son for evaluation of erectile dysfunction. He has been unable to achieve an erection for six months, since starting a new medicine. His history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.8%), and major depression after his wife died eight months ago. He takes metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and sertraline 100 mg daily, started six months ago. Blood pressure is 128/76 and heart rate is 62. Which principle should guide medication assessment before choosing a replacement antidepressant?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment has increasing confusion over two weeks. His family reports good medication adherence. He takes metformin, amlodipine, losartan, and recently added trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a urinary tract infection, now on day five of seven. Potassium is 5.8, creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.3), glucose 142, and blood pressure 128/76. Which medication-review plan best addresses the drug interaction relevant to his laboratory findings?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment, diabetes, and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52) reports chronic constipation at her annual visit. Medications are metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and pravastatin 20 mg daily. Increasing fiber and fluids has not helped. Her daughter reports recent use of ibuprofen 400 mg daily for joint pain. Examination and CBC are normal. Which statement about ibuprofen and constipation follows Hazzard's discussion of NSAIDs?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with stable coronary disease, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) had his last myocardial infarction three years ago. He takes aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metformin 1000 mg twice daily. LDL is 72 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.8%. His wife reports missed evening doses. Which prescribing approach directly addresses the regimen-complexity problem described by Hazzard?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman living alone has unintentionally lost 8 lb over six months. Her appetite has declined and food no longer tastes the same. She takes lisinopril, metformin, sertraline, and omeprazole; BMI is 20 kg/m2. Which approach incorporates the nutritional screening and medication review described in Hazzard?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes, coronary artery disease, and depression presents with dizziness and weakness. He takes metformin, atorvastatin, metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, lisinopril, paroxetine 40 mg daily, and recently added amitriptyline 75 mg for neuropathy. BP is 102/68 seated and 84/52 standing, heart rate is 58, and QTc is 492 ms. Which assessment of amitriptyline follows from the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · A 76-year-old woman presents for Mohs surgery for a 1.2-cm basal cell carcinoma on the tip of her nose. She reports increasing difficulty managing her finances and has missed two appointments. Her daughter confirms that she has recently forgotten to pay bills. Her MMSE score is 22/30. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Which statement about Mohs surgery in older adults is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · A 68-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and mild depression reports reduced sexual satisfaction and difficulty with arousal. She takes metformin, lisinopril, and sertraline and feels embarrassed discussing the problem. Which initial communication and assessment approach is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman who often misses meals has a severe hypoglycemic episode while taking glipizide and metformin. After immediate correction, repeat renal testing shows a stable eGFR of 27 mL/min/1.73 m². Which plan addresses both medication hazards?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and mild dementia has weight loss and frequent falls. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, and aspirin 81 mg. BMI fell from 23 to 19 over 8 months; HbA1c is 6.4% and LDL is 68. She forgets meals and struggles with cooking. Grip strength is 14 kg, and she rises slowly while holding furniture. Which adjustment addresses the hypoglycemia risk emphasized by Hazzard?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with NYHA class II heart failure, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment wants to begin exercising. He lives alone, has fallen twice in the past year, and takes metformin, lisinopril, and metoprolol. His daughter is concerned about safety. Which approach best applies Hazzard's exercise principles?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment has fallen twice in the past month and now needs help with finances and medications. She takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. Blood pressure falls from 150/85 supine to 125/75 standing; her get-up-and-go test is abnormal and MMSE is 22/30. Which approach addresses her multiple fall-risk domains?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman has recurrent falls over six months and takes 14 seconds on the Alternate Step Test. She takes lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and recently started solifenacin 5 mg daily. She has difficulty judging curb height despite corrected acuity of 20/25 in each eye. Hazzard recommends a Pelli-Robson chart as part of low-vision assessment. Which visual function does this chart assess?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with diabetes takes metformin. Her eGFR has fallen to 28 mL/min/1.73 m². Considering the renal appropriateness of metformin separately from treatment of congestion, which action follows Hazzard?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and type 2 diabetes has nocturia that disrupts sleep. He takes metformin, tamsulosin, and trazodone. Examination shows no prostatic nodules; urinalysis shows glucosuria without other abnormalities, and glycemic control is poor. His wife asks about desmopressin. Which approach addresses the metabolic contributor described by Hazzard?

Practice · An 85-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia becomes disoriented, pulls at his oxygen cannula, and tries to leave bed after 36 hours without sleep. He is oriented to person only. Home medications are tamsulosin, metformin, and lisinopril. Temperature is 37.8 degrees C, pulse 92, blood pressure 135/80 mm Hg, respiratory rate 22, and oxygen saturation 91% on 2 L/min. His daughter says he would want everything done. Which initial supportive approach accompanies evaluation and treatment of his acute illness?

Practice · An older patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease takes metformin and has an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 32 mL/min/1.73 m². Which monitoring principle is consistent with Hazzard?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment develops fatigue, difficulty shopping and a postural blood-pressure fall after starting amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. She also takes metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin and aspirin. Which change best addresses the new symptoms?

Practice · An older adult develops delirium on the second day after hip surgery. He receives morphine PCA and metformin despite an eGFR of 22 mL/min/1.73 m². In addition to evaluating infection, hypoxia, retention, metabolic disturbance and pain, which medication plan is appropriate?

Practice · An 83-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and diabetes presents with fatigue and poor oral intake. His daughter manages his metformin and glimepiride. Sodium is 156, glucose 680, and calculated effective serum osmolality about 350 mOsm/kg. She has also given him her furosemide for swelling. Which renal mechanism can link uncontrolled hyperglycemia to the water deficit, without establishing its contribution relative to poor intake or diuretic exposure?

Practice · A 75-year-old woman with early Alzheimer disease (MMSE 24) and diabetes attends a routine review. She lives alone, drives short distances, and uses a pillbox filled weekly by her daughter. HbA1c is 9.2%, compared with 7.8% six months earlier. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily and glipizide 10 mg twice daily. Her daughter has found glucose tablets around the home and reports morning shakiness. During a review of possible hypoglycemia, which change removes a hypoglycemia-risk drug while individualizing her treatment goals?

Practice · A 73-year-old woman with diabetes and a recent hip replacement has recurrent sudden episodes of syncope lasting 1–2 minutes, followed by full recovery. Her daughter observes pallor during events. Medications include metformin 1000 mg twice daily, apixaban 5 mg twice daily, and oxycodone/acetaminophen as needed. Orthostatic vital signs and the resting ECG are normal. Continuous monitoring records a 4.2-second sinus pause during syncope. Reversible and physiologic causes have been excluded. Which approach to permanent pacing follows Hazzard?

Practice · A 70-year-old woman with heart failure, diabetes, and arthritis reports that her medications are affecting sexual function. She takes metoprolol, furosemide, metformin, and gabapentin for neuropathic pain and asks about changing treatment. Which approach best reflects the source's discussion of medication-related sexual concerns in older women?

Practice · אישה בת 70 עם סוכרת מסוג 2 המאוזנת על metformin שואלת על clinical trials עתידיים המכוונים לתהליכי הזדקנות. היא מתעניינת ב-interventions שעשויים לשפר את תפקוד מערכת החיסון שלה ואת ה-healthspan הכולל. על בסיס המחקר הנוכחי, מה המנגנון העיקרי שבאמצעותו metformin עשוי לשפר את התגובה החיסונית במבוגרים?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, and depression has mixed urinary incontinence and incomplete emptying. Her medications include metformin, gabapentin, duloxetine, and recently added oxybutynin. Since oxybutynin was started, initiation of voiding has become difficult and postvoid residual has increased. Urodynamics shows detrusor underactivity. Which change addresses the bladder-relaxant risk described in Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with moderate dementia, diabetes, and hypertension is found on the floor, confused and sweating, with glucose 42 mg/dL. He lives alone with weekly family visits. He takes glimepiride 4 mg once daily with breakfast, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily; his recent HbA1c is 6.8%. After treatment with dextrose, which change removes the long-acting sulfonylurea exposure highlighted by the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with moderate dementia (MMSE 18), diabetes, and benign prostatic hyperplasia has daily urinary leakage for three weeks. He takes donepezil 10 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. His bladder is palpable to the umbilicus; anal tone is normal and stool is present in the rectal vault. Postvoid residual is 450 mL and creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL, up from 1.2. Which approach addresses urinary retention?

Practice · An 81-year-old with stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22) is under observation for an acute subdural hematoma. Oral intake is unpredictable and glucose is persistently 250–300 mg/dL. She takes metformin and glipizide. Which inpatient plan best limits medication-related harm while treating hyperglycemia?

Practice · A 76-year-old with cognitive impairment forgets tablets and takes glyburide 10 mg twice daily and metformin. Her A1C is 9.2% and creatinine clearance is 48 mL/min. Which step should guide the next treatment plan?

Practice · An 81-year-old assisted-living resident with moderate vascular dementia, diabetes, and osteoarthritis now needs help bathing and dressing, has fallen twice in the past month, and sometimes misses medication. She takes metformin 500 mg twice daily, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, and acetaminophen as needed; HbA1c is 8.2% and creatinine clearance is 38 mL/min. Which description matches the GRACE model being considered to coordinate her care?

Practice · A 76-year-old woman with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has recurrent hypoglycemia while taking metformin, glipizide, and insulin according to glucose readings. The acute episode has been treated. Her eGFR is stable at 38 mL/min/1.73 m2, without acute illness or impaired perfusion. What should be the focus of medication adjustment to prevent recurrence?

Practice · An 82-year-old man in a nursing facility for rehabilitation after a recent left middle cerebral artery stroke with residual hemiparesis develops acute confusion and agitation during dinner. Staff observed food pocketing and failure to swallow before he became aggressive when they tried to help. He has diabetes and hypertension and takes aspirin, lisinopril, metformin, and mirtazapine 15 mg at bedtime. Oxygen saturation falls to 88%, and chest radiography shows a right lower-lobe infiltrate. Which source-described relationship makes a swallowing-related pulmonary complication relevant?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with moderate vascular dementia, diabetes, and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m2) has become aggressive, strikes caregivers, and has refused medication for a week. She takes metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg. Her daughter requests nursing-home placement for safety. Physical examination shows no evidence of acute illness. Which medication-safety and diagnostic assessment is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension presents after a mechanical fall. She takes metformin, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and aspirin. BP is 142/88 and glucose is 52. She reports recurrent dizziness and near-falls. Creatinine is 1.3, eGFR 44, and Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance 38 mL/min. After treating the hypoglycemia, which assessment of glyburide accords with the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · A 79-year-old man has localized prostate cancer (Gleason 3+4, PSA 8.2), type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.8%), and stage 3b CKD (eGFR 42; Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance 38 mL/min). He uses a walker after a recent hip fracture and has ECOG performance status 2. His medications are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, and alendronate 70 mg weekly. Estimated life expectancy is 6 years. After discussion, he chooses to defer cancer treatment until symptomatic disease develops, rather than plan delayed curative treatment. Which strategy describes this choice?

Practice · A 68-year-old man reports six months of erectile dysfunction. He has no known cardiovascular disease but experiences intermittent chest discomfort with exertion, which he attributes to aging. He takes metformin for type 2 diabetes diagnosed three years ago. Blood pressure is 145/92 mmHg and BMI is 32. Which evaluation addresses the concern raised by this combination before proceeding with erectile-dysfunction treatment?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes and stage 3a chronic kidney disease is hospitalized for pneumonia. On the third day he develops new confusion, difficulty following commands and picking at the sheets; his wife reports that he was cognitively clear the day before. Medications include metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, ceftriaxone and as-needed diphenhydramine for sleep. Which approach fits the medication component of delirium management?

Practice · A 78-year-old man has type 2 diabetes, hypertension, COPD, and stage 3 CKD (eGFR 45 mL/min). He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg daily, lisinopril 40 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, tiotropium, and simvastatin 20 mg daily.
